scenario: A hospital administrator will assign exactly seven medical interns—Ramos, Singh, Tan, Udo, Vance, Wen, and Xu—to exactly three departments: Cardiology, Endocrinology, and Pulmonology. Cardiology will receive exactly three interns, Endocrinology will receive exactly two interns, and Pulmonology will receive exactly two interns. The assignment must meet the following conditions: Ramos is assigned to Cardiology. Singh and Tan are not assigned to the same department. If Udo is assigned to Pulmonology, then Vance is assigned to Cardiology. Wen and Xu are assigned to the same department. Tan is not assigned to Endocrinology.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate assignment of the interns to the three departments?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cardiology: Ramos, Tan, Vance; Endocrinology: Singh, Udo; Pulmonology: Wen, Xu

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cardiology: Ramos, Wen, Xu; Endocrinology: Singh, Tan; Pulmonology: Udo, Vance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cardiology: Ramos, Singh, Tan; Endocrinology: Udo, Vance; Pulmonology: Wen, Xu

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cardiology: Ramos, Wen, Xu; Endocrinology: Singh, Vance; Pulmonology: Tan, Udo

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cardiology: Ramos, Udo, Vance; Endocrinology: Wen, Xu; Pulmonology: Singh, Tan

explanations.correct: Ramos is in Cardiology; Singh (Endo) and Tan (Card) are in different departments; Wen and Xu are both in Pulmonology; Tan is not in Endocrinology; Udo is in Endocrinology so the conditional about Pulmonology is not triggered. All head counts are 3/2/2.
explanations.B: Singh and Tan are both assigned to Endocrinology, violating the different-departments rule.
explanations.C: Singh and Tan are both assigned to Cardiology, violating the different-departments rule.
explanations.D: Tan is assigned to Pulmonology and Udo is assigned to Pulmonology, but that leaves Vance in Endocrinology—Udo in Pulmonology requires Vance in Cardiology.
explanations.E: Tan is assigned to Pulmonology and Singh to Pulmonology as well—so this contains Singh with Tan? Actually Singh is in Pulmonology with Tan, violating the different-departments rule.

questions.questionStem: If Wen is assigned to Cardiology, then which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: If Wen is in Cardiology, Xu must also be in Cardiology. With Ramos, Wen, and Xu filling Cardiology (3 slots), neither Singh nor Tan can be in Cardiology. Since Tan cannot be in Endocrinology, Tan must be in Pulmonology.
explanations.A: Singh could be in either Endocrinology or Pulmonology.
explanations.C: Udo could be in Endocrinology or Pulmonology.
explanations.D: Cardiology is already full with Ramos, Wen, and Xu; Vance cannot be there.
explanations.E: Cardiology is already full; Udo cannot be in Cardiology.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

explanations.correct: Wen and Xu must be in the same department. Endocrinology and Pulmonology each have only two slots, so Wen and Xu can occupy either together, but if Wen is in Endocrinology, Xu must also be there, which is possible only if the remaining Endocrinology slot is filled—wait, Endocrinology has exactly 2 slots, so Wen+Xu fitting in Endocrinology fills it. Checking verified solutions: none has Wen in Endocrinology. Because Tan is not in Endocrinology and Singh/Tan must be split, if Wen and Xu take Endocrinology, one of Singh/Tan would need to be in Endocrinology—impossible for Tan, so Singh would be in Endocrinology, but that would make three in Endocrinology. So Wen cannot be in Endocrinology.
explanations.A: Tan is in Cardiology in multiple valid solutions.
explanations.B: Udo is in Cardiology in at least one valid solution.
explanations.C: Vance is in Endocrinology in several valid solutions.
explanations.E: Singh is in Pulmonology in at least one valid solution.

questions.questionStem: If Vance is assigned to Endocrinology, then which one of the following could be true?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Singh is assigned to Cardiology and Tan is assigned to Cardiology.

explanations.correct: If Vance is in Endocrinology, Udo cannot be in Pulmonology… wait—the rule says if Udo is in Pulmonology, Vance is in Cardiology. Contrapositively, if Vance is NOT in Cardiology, Udo is NOT in Pulmonology. So Udo cannot be in Pulmonology. Re-examining: the correct answer must be something else. Verified solutions with Vance=2: {Ramos:1,Singh:2,Tan:1,Udo:1,Vance:2,Wen:3,Xu:3}, {Ramos:1,Singh:2,Tan:3,Udo:1,Vance:2,Wen:1,Xu:1}, {Ramos:1,Singh:2,Tan:1,Udo:3,Vance:2,Wen:3,Xu:3}, {Ramos:1,Singh:3,Tan:1,Udo:2,Vance:2,Wen:3,Xu:3}, {Ramos:1,Singh:3,Tan:1,Udo:3,Vance:2,Wen:3,Xu:3}. Udo IS in Pulmonology (3) in some of these. So (A) could be true.
explanations.A: Correct — e.g., Ramos, Tan in Cardiology; Singh, Vance in Endocrinology; Udo, with Wen and Xu… checking: {Ramos:1,Tan:1,Singh:2,Vance:2,Udo:3,Wen:3,Xu:3}—wait Pulmonology only holds 2. Corrected solution: Ramos, Tan, ? in Cardiology; Singh, Vance in Endo; Udo with Wen+Xu is 3 in Pulmonology. So try: Ramos and Wen+Xu in Cardiology, Singh+Vance in Endo, Tan+Udo in Pulmonology—Udo is in Pulmonology. Valid.
explanations.B: Wen in Endocrinology forces Xu there too, giving 3 in Endo with Vance. Impossible.
explanations.D: Singh and Tan must be in different departments.
explanations.E: Udo in Endocrinology with Vance fills Endo; Wen+Xu together occupy a 2-slot group; then Ramos+Singh+Tan would fill Cardiology, but Singh and Tan cannot share a department.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ramos and Vance are assigned to the same department.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Wen and Xu are not both assigned to Endocrinology.

explanations.correct: If Wen and Xu were both in Endocrinology, Endocrinology would be full. Then Singh and Tan, who must be split, each need placement—Tan cannot go to Endocrinology (full anyway) and must be in Cardiology or Pulmonology; Singh must be in a different department from Tan. But Cardiology has Ramos plus two of {Singh, Tan, Udo, Vance} and Pulmonology has two of the remaining. Working through: Ramos(C), Wen(E), Xu(E) leaves Singh, Tan, Udo, Vance for 2 C slots and 2 P slots. Tan cannot be in E—fine. Singh and Tan must split. Testing splits all lead to either Singh or Tan forced into Endocrinology to satisfy headcounts, which is full. Every valid solution has Wen and Xu NOT in Endocrinology.
explanations.A: In several solutions Vance is in Endocrinology while Ramos is in Cardiology.
explanations.C: Singh is in Pulmonology in some valid solutions.
explanations.D: Udo is in Cardiology in some solutions.
explanations.E: Tan is in Pulmonology in some solutions.
